1	# Screen recording
2	
3	Frame Job records your screen itself. You can record a whole display or a single window, with system audio, your microphone and rings around your clicks, and the recording goes straight into a project. You can also record a camera, on its own or beside the screen as a talking head in the corner, and a voice-over, which is the microphone alone with no picture, at the playhead of the project you're editing. Every recording is an ordinary movie or audio file on disk, and Frame Job imports it the way it imports any other media, so every edit, effect and export works on it.
4	
5	## Opening the recorder
6	
7	Choose **File ▸ New Recording…** (⌥⌘N), or click **New Recording…** on the welcome window. A small floating panel titled **New Recording** opens. You don't need a project open.
8	
9	The panel floats above other windows and doesn't make Frame Job the active app when you click it. That lets you bring the app you want to record to the front and still press Record. It also doesn't hide when you switch to another app. If you open it while Frame Job is in the background, it comes to the front without taking the keyboard, so your typing stays in the app you were using.
10	
11	In the panel, Return presses **Record** and Esc presses **Close**.
12	
13	## The panel's controls
14	
15	| Control | What it does | Default |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| **Source** | What to record. Lists one row per connected display by name, then **Window…** (pick one window), then **Camera** (a camera on its own), then **Microphone Only** (a voice-over with no picture). | The display you used last, else the main display |
18	| **Include Frame Job windows** | Puts Frame Job's own windows, such as the editor and the preview, into a display recording. When it's off, they're left out of the picture. | Off |
19	| **Record the camera too** | With a display or **Window…** as the source, also records the chosen camera beside the screen (see [A camera beside the screen](#a-camera-beside-the-screen)). It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**. | Off |
20	| **Camera** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, which camera to record: each connected camera by name, or **None connected**. An iPhone used as a Continuity Camera reads "<name> (Continuity Camera)". It's greyed out otherwise. | The camera you used last, else the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected |
21	| **Format** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, the size and frame rate to record at. **Best** comes first and names the camera's best format, for example **Best (1760×1328 at 30 fps)**. Then come the camera's other formats, such as **1920×1080 at 30 fps**: sizes wider than tall first, then square, then taller than wide, each largest first and at its highest frame rate. It's greyed out otherwise. | The format you used last when the chosen camera has it, else Best |
22	| **Preview** | With **Source** set to **Camera**, or with **Record the camera too** ticked, a live picture of the chosen camera at the chosen format, under Format. It's shown as the movie will record it: not mirrored, the whole picture fitted inside. The row appears only then. | — |
23	| **Layout** | With **Record the camera too** ticked, where the camera lands beside the screen: **Corner**, **Rounded Corner**, **Circle**, **Side by Side** or **Camera Full** (see [A camera beside the screen](#a-camera-beside-the-screen)). It's greyed out, keeping its value, without the box, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, or while a recording is under way. | Corner |
24	| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | With **Record the camera too** ticked, runs **Clip ▸ Remove Background** on the camera's clips once they land, as its own undo step. Greyed out, keeping its value, as Layout is. | Off |
25	| **Microphone** | **Off**, or one of the connected microphones. A live level meter sits beside it. | Off |
26	| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | After the recording lands, runs [Enhance Voice](audio.md#enhance-voice) on the microphone's clips (see [Enhancing the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone)). It works with any source, and it's greyed out, keeping its value, when **Microphone** is **Off** or a recording is under way. | Off |
27	| **System Audio** | Records what the system plays, as the movie's own stereo 48 kHz sound track. | On |
28	| **Cursor** | **Separate** keeps the pointer and the click ring out of the movie: the recording's cursor file records them, and Frame Job draws the pointer on the clip, where its **Cursor** section can restyle it (see [The cursor](#the-cursor)). **In the picture** lets macOS draw the pointer into the movie, as before. It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**. | **Separate** |
29	| **Show Clicks** | With Cursor **In the picture**, draws a ring around each mouse click into the movie. With Cursor **Separate**, nothing is drawn into the movie: the recording's clips land with click ripples turned on (**Clicks: Ripple** in their Cursor section). | Off |
30	| **Record shortcuts** | With a display or **Window…** as the source, writes each keyboard shortcut you press into the recording's cursor files, and when you type, but never what you type (see [Shortcuts and Input Monitoring](#shortcuts-and-input-monitoring)). Needs the **Input Monitoring** permission. A note under it says what it records. It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**. | Off |
31	| **Zoom in on clicks** | Under **When it lands:**. After the recording lands, runs [Auto Zoom](#auto-zoom) on its screen clips (see [When it lands](#when-it-lands)). It's greyed out, keeping its value, with **Camera** or **Microphone Only**, or while a recording is under way. | On |
32	| **Show shortcuts** | After the recording lands, runs [Add Shortcut Overlays](#shortcut-overlays) on its screen clips. It's live only with **Record shortcuts** ticked, and greyed out, keeping its value, otherwise. | On (with Record shortcuts) |
33	| **Speed up typing** | After the recording lands, runs [Speed Up Typing](#speeding-up-typing) on its screen clips once their speech is detected. It's live only with **Record shortcuts** ticked, and greyed out, keeping its value, otherwise. | Off |
34	| **Rate** | **30 fps** or **60 fps**: the most frames per second the file may hold. It's also the frame rate of a new project made from the recording. | 60 fps |
35	| **Size** | **Nominal (points)** records the display at its point size. **Best (pixels)** records every pixel, which is twice the points on a Retina display. | Nominal (points) |
36	| **Record Into** | **New Project**, or any open project by name. | The front project, else New Project |
37	
38	Under Size, a note shows what you'll get for the chosen display, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels`. For a picked window it reads "the picked window's own size". For Microphone Only it reads "no picture — the microphone alone". For Camera it names the format the camera records at, for example `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` with Format set to Best, `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen format` with a format chosen, or "no camera connected".
39	
40	The footnote at the bottom left shows where recordings are saved (for example `saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`). While a recording runs, it shows the elapsed time instead.
41	
42	The panel remembers your choices between uses, including the display, microphone, camera, camera format, switches, rate, size and the Include Frame Job windows, Record the camera too, Enhance the microphone when it lands, Record shortcuts, Zoom in on clicks, Show shortcuts and Speed up typing boxes, the camera's **Layout** and the Remove the camera's background box. It remembers **Cursor** only once you choose it: until then it shows Separate, and a choice you make holds for every source. The camera format is one choice for every camera: a camera that doesn't have the remembered format shows Best. It doesn't remember a picked window, the Camera or Microphone Only source (each lasts for the session only), or Record Into. A display, microphone or camera that is no longer connected falls back to the main display, to Off, or to the default camera. While the panel is up and not recording, the Camera and Microphone lists follow the devices you plug in or take away (a change made during a recording waits for it to end). A camera that's removed falls back to the default camera, and when it comes back it's chosen again with its format. Plugging in or removing a device doesn't change what the panel remembers.
43	
44	### Record Into
45	
46	**Record Into** follows whichever project is in front, until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open. When you press Record, the row freezes, so switching to another window during the recording doesn't change where the recording goes.
47	
48	## Choosing what to record
49	
50	### A display
51	
52	Choose a display by name in **Source**. Frame Job's own windows are left out of a display recording unless **Include Frame Job windows** is on. Even with the box on, the recorder panel itself is never in the picture. The panel leaves the screen as soon as the recording starts.
53	
54	Frame Job's own sound is never recorded, with or without the box. That means you can play the timeline during a recording and it won't end up in the file.
55	
56	### A window
57	
58	Choose **Window…** in **Source** and macOS's window picker opens. Click the window you want. The Source row then reads **Window (picked)** and the recording is that window alone, at its own size. If you cancel the picker, Source goes back to the display you used last. If the picker can't open at all, Source also goes back to the display you used last, and the note reads "The window picker could not open: …" with the reason.
59	
60	When **Include Frame Job windows** is off, the picker lists none of Frame Job's windows. When it's on, the picker lists them, but never the recorder panel. The box only changes the next time the picker opens. A window you've already picked stays picked.
61	
62	If you press Record while the row reads **Window…** with nothing picked, the panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display." and nothing records.
63	
64	### A camera
65	
66	Choose **Camera** in **Source**, then the camera in **Camera**:
67	
68	- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** grey out. Their values are kept for next time. A camera records at the format chosen in **Format**, at that format's highest frame rate. **Best** is the largest size wider than tall that runs at 30 fps or more. The note under Size names the format.
69	- **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live. The microphone you choose, which can be the camera's own when macOS lists it, is recorded to its own file beside the movie. **Off** records the camera alone.
70	- With no camera connected, Record says "No camera is connected."
71	- Only the Camera permission (and the Microphone permission, when one is chosen) is checked. Screen Recording isn't needed.
72	
73	The camera starts as soon as the panel shows **Camera**, and the **Preview** under Format shows its live picture. Because it's already running, it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing a display or another source (unless **Record the camera too** is ticked there), or closing the panel, turns it off. The preview changes with the camera and format you choose. Instead of the picture it reads "No camera is connected." with no camera, "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." until you've allowed the Camera permission (showing the panel never asks for it, pressing Record does), or the reason the camera couldn't start. Choosing **Camera** again or reopening the panel tries again. **The panel stays up** while a camera records, as it does for a voice-over: nothing on screen is filmed. Its controls lock, the meter stays live, the footnote shows ● or ❚❚ and the elapsed time, Record reads **Stop**, and a **Pause** / **Resume** button appears beside it. If you close the panel, the recording carries on.
74	
75	The camera's movie lands like a screen recording's picture: on the front track if it fits, else on a new track in front, with the microphone on a new back track named **Microphone**. As a new project, the canvas is the movie's size at the format's frame rate. If the camera stops on its own (for example, it's unplugged), the recording ends there, what was captured lands, and the note gives the reason followed by "What was captured was added." If the camera hadn't settled at its frame rate when recording began, the note says what rate it ran at.
76	
77	### A camera beside the screen
78	
79	Choose a display or **Window…** in **Source**, tick **Record the camera too**, then choose the camera in **Camera** and its size and frame rate in **Format**. Frame Job records the screen and the camera at the same time, for a talking head over a screencast:
80	
81	- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows** and **Rate** stay live and apply to the screen. The note under Size describes the screen.
82	- The camera starts as soon as the box is ticked, and the **Preview** under Format shows its live picture, so it has settled at its frame rate by the time recording begins. Unticking the box, choosing **Microphone Only**, or closing the panel turns it off.
83	- With no camera connected, Record says "No camera is connected."
84	- Pressing Record checks the Screen Recording permission, then the Camera permission, then the Microphone permission when one is chosen, then counts down.
85	- The panel leaves the screen as for any screen recording, and the menu-bar item is its only control.
86	
87	The recording lands as `record_screen` with `camera` lands it (see [For agents](#for-agents-record_screen)): each stretch's camera movie, named after its screen movie with ` (Camera)` added, goes on one new track named **Camera** in front of everything, lined up with the screen, and is laid out in the panel's **Layout**, as **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸** lays it out with the stretch's screen clip:
88	
89	- **Corner** (the default) puts the camera in the bottom-right corner, scaled to fit a box a quarter of the canvas wide and a third of it tall, inside the 90 % guide of **View ▸ Safe Areas**. **Rounded Corner** and **Circle** are the same corner with rounded edges or a circle. **Side by Side** puts the screen and the camera next to each other, and **Camera Full** fills the canvas with the camera.
90	- The layout starts at the camera clip's first frame. The screen keeps its full picture until the camera arrives, and the layout reaches no further than that stretch's screen clip or its camera clip, so a clip that was already in the project never moves, and another stretch's screen without a camera stays full.
91	- If a stretch's screen clip isn't playing where its camera starts, that camera goes in the bottom-right corner instead.
92	- With **Remove the camera's background when it lands** ticked, the camera's clips then get **Clip ▸ Remove Background** as their own undo step, **Remove Background**, before any [Enhance the microphone](#enhancing-the-microphone) and the boxes under [When it lands](#when-it-lands). Edit ▸ Undo takes it off and keeps the recording.
93	
94	Each camera clip stays an ordinary clip: you can move it, or choose another layout from **Clip ▸ Camera Layout ▸**. If a tool records a camera beside the screen while the panel is up, the panel's **Preview** reads "The camera is recording." until it ends.
95

97	
98	See [Voice-overs](#voice-overs-microphone-only) below.

3	/// The panel SHOWN: `show()`, the one-second timer that keeps the Record Into
4	/// rows current while it is up, `setNote` and the refit that keeps the card on
5	/// its screen — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s ninth file. A pure move out
6	/// of the base file, which stood at 399 lines against the 400-line cap a
7	/// Camera source would have grown: camera recording's CR1-0, paid first and
8	/// alone. Its `// MARK: - Showing` came here whole, bodies untouched;
9	/// `armSyncTimer` stays private, since its one caller, `show()`, moved with it.
10	extension RecorderPanelController {
11	
12	    // MARK: - Showing
13	
14	    /// Beeps and shows nothing while a recording has the panel hidden (the
15	    /// type doc): the welcome window's button is the caller that would
16	    /// otherwise un-hide it into the recording. Shown while idle, a prepared
17	    /// capture that failed (or a build that threw) is let go first, so the
18	    /// preview's sync tries again (spec §11 CAM-7 (5)). The device observers
19	    /// are added before that sync, which applies a change made while the
20	    /// panel was closed (CAM-8 (1)).
21	    func show() {
22	        guard !hiddenForRecording else {
23	            NSSound.beep()
24	            return
25	        }
26	        panelClosing = false
27	        if phase == .idle {
28	            rebuildSources()
29	            rebuildMicrophones()
30	            rebuildCameras()
31	            restoreChoices()
32	            if recorder.state == .idle, previewFailure != nil { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
33	        }
34	        rebuildDestinations()
35	        refreshSizeNote()
36	        fitWindowToContent()
37	        floatAgain()
38	        if NSApp.isActive {
39	            showWindow(nil)
40	            window?.makeKeyAndOrderFront(nil)
41	        } else {
42	            window?.orderFrontRegardless()
43	        }
44	        armSyncTimer()
45	        observeDevices()
46	        syncCameraPreview()
47	    }
48	
49	    /// One second, while the panel is up: the Record Into rows follow the
50	    /// documents that open and close and the one in front — while idle,
51	    /// which `rebuildDestinations` itself decides — and the camera preview
52	    /// steps again (CAM-7 (5)).
53	    private func armSyncTimer() {
54	        guard syncTimer == nil else { return }
55	        syncTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(withTimeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
56	            guard let self else {
57	                timer.invalidate()
58	                return
59	            }
60	            guard self.window?.isVisible == true else { return }
61	            self.rebuildDestinations()
62	            self.syncCameraPreview()
63	        }
64	    }
65	
66	    // `syncPhase()` and `refreshStatusLabel()` — the phases drawn — are
67	    // `+Pause.swift`'s since the R2 review, the base file's toll.
68	
69	    func setNote(_ text: String) {
70	        noteLabel.stringValue = text
71	        noteLabel.isHidden = text.isEmpty
72	        fitWindowToContent()
73	    }
74	
75	    /// The window takes the card's fitting size, keeping its TOP-LEFT where
76	    /// it was — `setContentSize` would keep the bottom-left and walk the
77	    /// title bar up the screen every time the note appeared — and then
78	    /// CONSTRAINED to its screen (`window.screen`, else the main one), so a
79	    /// panel whose bottom edge sits near the Dock is pushed up when the
80	    /// countdown grows it rather than growing under the Dock (R1 review;
81	    /// measured, the numeral adds 88 pt below the rows and a note 42 more).
82	    /// `setFrame` itself constrains nothing — a window can be put anywhere
83	    /// programmatically, on screen or off — which is why the call is
84	    /// explicit.
85	    func fitWindowToContent() {
86	        guard let window else { return }
87	        card.layoutSubtreeIfNeeded()
88	        let content = NSRect(origin: .zero, size: card.fittingSize)
89	        var frame = window.frameRect(forContentRect: content)
90	        let current = window.frame
91	        frame.origin = NSPoint(x: current.minX, y: current.maxY - frame.height)
92	        let screen = window.screen ?? NSScreen.main ?? NSScreen.screens.first
93	        frame = window.constrainFrameRect(frame, to: screen)
94	        window.setFrame(frame, display: window.isVisible)
95	    }
96	}

3	/// The Source row "Microphone Only" — a VOICE-OVER from the panel (#99;
4	/// spec §11 recording, "A voice-over is a recording with no picture") —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eighth file, NEW rather than cut: it is
6	/// the whole of what the panel adds for a recording with no picture, and the
7	/// base file, `+Rows.swift` and `+Recording.swift` learn it only by a line or
8	/// two each.
9	///
10	/// **The row** is the Source popup's last, directly under "Camera" (tag 3,
11	/// `+Camera.swift`, which sits under "Window…"), by tag.
12	/// It persists for the session only, as a picked window does: no defaults key
13	/// is written for it, and the display key is left alone while it is chosen.
14	/// Chosen, it greys System Audio, Show Clicks and Size with their values
15	/// KEPT, so the panel does not jump under the pointer; Rate stays live (it is
16	/// a new project's rate), and so do Microphone and Record Into.
17	///
18	/// **The press** never reads or asks the Screen Recording grant: Microphone
19	/// "Off" refuses with a note, and otherwise the Microphone grant is the only
20	/// one checked (`+Grants.swift`'s `checkMicrophoneGrant`, the panel's one
21	/// door to it) before the same 3-2-1. The start is `startVoiceOver`, which
22	/// answers before it returns — there is no lookup and no arming, so no start
23	/// timer either.
24	///
25	/// **The panel STAYS UP while it records** (the owner's choice): the rows are
26	/// locked as for any recording, the meter is live, the footnote shows the dot
27	/// or the pause glyph and the elapsed time, Record reads Stop, and a Pause /
28	/// Resume button stands beside it. `hidesForRecording` is the one decision
29	/// `recordingDidStart` reads; Close takes the panel away and the recording
30	/// carries on under the status item. A camera recording stays up on the same
31	/// terms (spec §11 CAM-5), so the decision and the button cover it too.
32	extension RecorderPanelController {
33	    /// The Source row, by tag: last, directly under "Camera" (tag 3), which
34	    /// sits under "Window…" (tag 1), with no separator between them.
35	    static let voiceOverTag = 2
36	    static let microphoneOnlyTitle = "Microphone Only"
37	    static let microphoneOffSentence =
38	        "Microphone Only records the microphone alone — choose a microphone first."
39	    static let voiceOverSizeNote = "no picture — the microphone alone"
40	
41	    var voiceOverSelected: Bool { sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.voiceOverTag }
42	
43	    /// Whether the panel orders out at `recordingDidStart` for `source`:
44	    /// not for a voice-over or a camera, which film nothing on screen.
45	    static func hidesForRecording(_ source: RecordingSource) -> Bool { source != .voiceOver && source != .camera }
46	
47	    /// Every control unlocked only while idle; the six screen-only ones
48	    /// (Include Frame Job windows among them, set only here, Record
49	    /// shortcuts, spec §11 CU-62, and Cursor, CU-36) greyed besides
50	    /// while Microphone Only is chosen, their values kept; then the camera's
51	    /// locks (`syncCameraControls`), last.
52	    func syncControlsEnabled() {
53	        let idle = phase == .idle
54	        let controls: [NSControl] = [
55	            sourcePopup, microphonePopup, ratePopup, sizePopup, destinationPopup,
56	            systemAudioSwitch, showClicksSwitch, recordShortcutsCheckbox,
57	            cursorPopup,
58	        ]
59	        for control in controls { control.isEnabled = idle }
60	        let screenOnly = idle && !voiceOverSelected
61	        let screenControls: [NSControl] = [
62	            systemAudioSwitch, showClicksSwitch, sizePopup, includeFrameJobCheckbox,
63	            recordShortcutsCheckbox,
64	            cursorPopup,
65	        ]
66	        for control in screenControls {
67	            control.isEnabled = screenOnly
68	        }
69	        // AU-69 (a): live only while idle with a microphone, on any source; greyed keeps its value.
70	        enhanceMicrophoneCheckbox.isEnabled = idle && currentChoice().microphone != nil
71	        syncCameraControls()
72	        syncPolishControls()
73	        syncCameraLandingControls()
74	    }
75	
76	    /// The Pause / Resume button beside Stop: on screen only while a
77	    /// voice-over or a camera records or is paused — a screen recording's
78	    /// panel is off screen, and its pause is the status item's.
79	    func syncPauseButton() {
80	        let live = phase == .recording || phase == .paused
81	        voiceOverPauseButton.isHidden = !((voiceOverSelected || cameraSelected) && live)
82	        let title = phase == .paused ? "Resume" : "Pause"
83	        if voiceOverPauseButton.title != title {
84	            voiceOverPauseButton.title = title
85	            voiceOverPauseButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    /// The button: pause while recording, resume while paused (the status
90	    /// item's own two calls, `+Pause.swift`); anything else beeps.
91	    @objc func pauseButtonPressed(_ sender: Any?) {
92	        switch phase {
93	        case .recording: pauseRecording()
94	        case .paused: resumeRecording()
95	        default: NSSound.beep()
96	        }
97	    }
98	
99	    /// Record with Microphone Only chosen: Off refuses with a note; otherwise
100	    /// the Microphone grant alone, then the countdown. Screen Recording is
101	    /// neither read nor asked.
102	    func beginVoiceOverIfGranted() {
103	        guard currentChoice().microphone != nil else {
104	            setNote(Self.microphoneOffSentence)
105	            return
106	        }
107	        floatAgain()
108	        guard checkMicrophoneGrant() else { return }
109	        setNote("")
110	        beginCountdown()
111	    }
112	
113	    /// The countdown's end for a voice-over: handed straight to the recorder,
114	    /// whose answer comes before it returns.
115	    func launchVoiceOver(_ choice: RecordingChoice) {
116	        launched = true
117	        recorder.startVoiceOver(
118	            choice: choice, mayAsk: true,
119	            onFinish: { [weak self] outcome in self?.recordingEnded(outcome) }
120	        ) { [weak self] error in
121	            guard let self else { return }
122	            if let error {
123	                self.startFailed(error)
124	                return
125	            }
126	            self.recordingDidStart()
127	        }
128	    }
129	}

4	/// The recorder panel's window picker (road map 3, R1c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s fifth file, cut out of `+Recording.swift`
6	/// along the line `presentPicker` draws when the R1 review's fixes put that
7	/// file past the 400-line cap. The Source row's last item, "Window…",
8	/// presents `SCContentSharingPicker` in single-window mode; the filter it
9	/// answers with is held in `pickedFilter` beside the choice (a filter is not
10	/// a value, so `.picked` is the one source that cannot persist), and a
11	/// cancel or a failure puts the Source row back on the display the person
12	/// last chose. Record with the row reading "Window…" and no filter held is
13	/// refused by name in `+Recording.swift`, never answered by presenting the
14	/// picker from the guard.
15	extension RecorderPanelController {
16	    // MARK: - The window picker
17	
18	    /// `SCContentSharingPicker` in single-window mode, what
19	    /// `recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows:)` names excluded from the
20	    /// LIST — Frame Job's application with Include Frame Job windows off, the
21	    /// panel's own window alone with it on (spec §11 recording.md).
22	    /// `excludedBundleIDs` is documented "for picking" and says nothing about
23	    /// capture (R0 q3), which is why R1 hid the panel for a picked window
24	    /// alone; since R2 every recording hides it (decision 7), and the
25	    /// exclusion is about the list only. The observer is added once; the
26	    /// picker is activated for the presentation and deactivated when it
27	    /// answers.
28	    func presentPicker() {
29	        let exclusion = recordingExclusion(
30	            includeFrameJobWindows: includeFrameJobCheckbox.state == .on)
31	        let picker = SCContentSharingPicker.shared
32	        if !pickerObserved {
33	            picker.add(self)
34	            pickerObserved = true
35	        }
36	        var configuration = SCContentSharingPickerConfiguration()
37	        configuration.allowedPickerModes = [.singleWindow]
38	        configuration.excludedBundleIDs = exclusion.bundleIDs
39	        configuration.excludedWindowIDs = exclusion.windowIDs.map { Int($0) }
40	        picker.defaultConfiguration = configuration
41	        picker.isActive = true
42	        picker.present(using: .window)
43	    }
44	
45	    /// What a display recording and the picker leave out (spec §11
46	    /// recording.md, Include Frame Job windows): Frame Job's application with
47	    /// the box off; with it on, the panel's own window, which is on screen
48	    /// until `recordingDidStart` — after the file's first frame (R0 q2).
49	    func recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows: Bool) -> RecordingExclusion {
50	        let number = window?.windowNumber ?? 0
51	        return RecordingExclusion.make(
52	            includeFrameJobWindows: includeFrameJobWindows,
53	            ownBundleID: Bundle.main.bundleIdentifier,
54	            panelWindowID: number > 0 ? CGWindowID(clamping: number) : nil)
55	    }
56	
57	    /// Back to the display the person last chose (the persisted one), with
58	    /// the Window row reading "Window…" again.
59	    private func revertSourceRow() {
60	        pickedFilter = nil
61	        sourcePopup.menu?.item(withTag: Self.windowTag)?.title = "Window…"
62	        let stored = UserDefaults.standard.integer(forKey: Self.displayKey)
63	        selectDisplay(stored > 0 ? CGDirectDisplayID(clamping: stored) : CGMainDisplayID())
64	        refreshSizeNote()
65	    }
66	}
67	
68	extension RecorderPanelController: SCContentSharingPickerObserver {
69	    /// The picker answers on a queue of its own; every arm hops to main.
70	    func contentSharingPicker(_ picker: SCContentSharingPicker, didCancelFor stream: SCStream?) {
71	        DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
72	            picker.isActive = false
73	            self?.revertSourceRow()
74	        }
75	    }
76	
77	    func contentSharingPicker(
78	        _ picker: SCContentSharingPicker, didUpdateWith filter: SCContentFilter, for stream: SCStream?
79	    ) {
80	        DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
81	            guard let self else { return }
82	            picker.isActive = false
83	            self.pickedFilter = filter
84	            self.sourcePopup.menu?.item(withTag: Self.windowTag)?.title = "Window (picked)"
85	            _ = self.sourcePopup.selectItem(withTag: Self.windowTag)
86	            self.refreshSizeNote()
87	            self.setNote("")
88	        }
89	    }
90	
91	    func contentSharingPickerStartDidFailWithError(_ error: any Error) {
92	        DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
93	            SCContentSharingPicker.shared.isActive = false
94	            self?.revertSourceRow()
95	            self?.setNote("The window picker could not open: " + error.localizedDescription)
96	        }
97	    }
98	}

30	/// stored `FrameJobRecordingCameraFormat` when the camera lists it, else
31	/// Best, and follows the Camera popup's live rule.
32	///
33	/// **The press** never reads or asks the Screen Recording grant: no camera
34	/// refuses with a note, then the Camera grant (`+Grants.swift`), then the
35	/// Microphone grant, then the same 3-2-1 — during which `beginCountdown`
36	/// prepares the camera's capture, so CAM-3's warm-up is spent there
37	/// (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`). The start is `startCamera`.
38	///
39	/// **The panel STAYS UP while a camera records** (the voice-over's
40	/// precedent, `hidesForRecording`): nothing on screen is filmed, so the rows
41	/// lock, the meter is live, and Record reads Stop with the Pause / Resume
42	/// button beside it.
43	///
44	/// **The live preview** under Format is `+CameraPreview.swift`'s (spec §11
45	/// CAM-7): its well, its step and its sync.
46	///
47	/// **"Record the camera too"** (CR3c, spec §11 CAM-11), a checkbox under
48	/// Include Frame Job windows, is live only while idle with a display row or
49	/// the Window row, and greyed with its value kept under Camera or Microphone
50	/// Only. Ticked, a camera is WANTED as with Source Camera: the Camera and
51	/// Format popups are live, the choice carries `camera` and `cameraFormat`
52	/// beside the screen source, and the preview shows. The five screen controls
53	/// stay live, and the press (`+Recording.swift`) reads Screen Recording, then
54	/// Camera, then Microphone.
55	extension RecorderPanelController {
56	    static let cameraTag = 3
57	    static let cameraTitle = "Camera"
58	    static let noCameraTitle = "None connected"
59	    static let bestFormatTitle = "Best"
60	
61	    var cameraSelected: Bool { sourcePopup.selectedItem?.tag == Self.cameraTag }
62	
63	    /// A display row or the Window row: the sources the box is live for.
64	    var screenSourceSelected: Bool { !voiceOverSelected && !cameraSelected }
65	
66	    /// "Record the camera too" ticked beside a screen source (CAM-11).
67	    var cameraBesideSelected: Bool { screenSourceSelected && cameraBesideCheckbox.state == .on }
68	
69	    /// Source Camera, or the box beside a screen source (CAM-11 (3)).
70	    var cameraWanted: Bool { cameraSelected || cameraBesideSelected }
71	
72	    /// The Camera popup's chosen `uniqueID`; nil for "None connected".
73	    var selectedCameraID: String? { cameraPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String }
74	
75	    /// The Format popup's chosen spelling; nil for Best.
76	    var selectedCameraFormat: String? { formatPopup.selectedItem?.representedObject as? String }
77	
78	    // MARK: - The popup
79	
80	    /// Every connected camera by name, carrying its `uniqueID`, or the one
81	    /// row "None connected"; the selection kept when it is still listed,
82	    /// else the default (`selectCamera`).
83	    func rebuildCameras() {
84	        let current = selectedCameraID
85	        cameraPopup.removeAllItems()
86	        let cameras = CameraDevices.connected()
87	        for camera in cameras {
88	            let item = NSMenuItem(
89	                title: CameraDevices.popupTitle(CameraDevices.facts(of: camera)), action: nil,
90	                keyEquivalent: "")
91	            item.representedObject = camera.uniqueID
92	            cameraPopup.menu?.addItem(item)
93	        }
94	        if cameras.isEmpty {
95	            cameraPopup.menu?.addItem(
96	                NSMenuItem(title: Self.noCameraTitle, action: nil, keyEquivalent: ""))
97	        }
98	        selectCamera(current)
99	    }
100	
101	    /// The row carrying `id`; nil, or an id no row carries, selects the
102	    /// default camera's row (CAM-3 (7): the system's preferred camera, else
103	    /// the first built-in, else the first), else the first row. The Format
104	    /// popup is rebuilt on every exit, the early one included (CAM-6 (2)).
105	    func selectCamera(_ id: String?) {
106	        defer { rebuildCameraFormats() }
107	        let rows = cameraPopup.itemArray
108	        if let id, let index = rows.firstIndex(where: { $0.representedObject as? String == id }) {
109	            cameraPopup.selectItem(at: index)
110	            return
111	        }
112	        let cameras = CameraDevices.connected().map(CameraDevices.facts(of:))
113	        let preferred = AVCaptureDevice.systemPreferredCamera?.uniqueID
114	        let wanted = CameraDevices.defaultIndex(in: cameras, preferredID: preferred).map {
115	            cameras[$0].uniqueID
116	        }
117	        let index =
118	            wanted.flatMap { wanted in
119	                rows.firstIndex { $0.representedObject as? String == wanted }
120	            } ?? 0
121	        if rows.indices.contains(index) { cameraPopup.selectItem(at: index) }
122	    }
123	
124	    // MARK: - The Format popup (CAM-6)
125	
126	    /// "Best (<the best format>)" — or "Best" when `camera` has none — then
127	    /// one row per `CameraDevices.formatRows` row, carrying its spelling;
128	    /// `stored` selected when a row carries it, else Best.
129	    func fillCameraFormats(_ camera: CameraDeviceFacts?, stored: String?) {
130	        formatPopup.removeAllItems()
131	        let formats = camera?.formats ?? []
132	        let best = camera.flatMap { CameraDevices.bestFormat($0.formats, active: $0.activeFormat) }
133	        let bestTitle =
134	            best.map { "\(Self.bestFormatTitle) (\(CameraDevices.formatTitle(formats[$0])))" }
135	            ?? Self.bestFormatTitle
136	        formatPopup.menu?.addItem(NSMenuItem(title: bestTitle, action: nil, keyEquivalent: ""))
137	        for index in CameraDevices.formatRows(formats) {
138	            let item = NSMenuItem(
139	                title: CameraDevices.formatTitle(formats[index]), action: nil, keyEquivalent: "")
140	            item.representedObject = CameraDevices.spelled(formats[index])
141	            formatPopup.menu?.addItem(item)
142	        }
143	        let index =
144	            stored.flatMap { stored in
145	                formatPopup.itemArray.firstIndex { $0.representedObject as? String == stored }
146	            } ?? 0
147	        formatPopup.selectItem(at: index)
148	    }
149	
150	    /// `fillCameraFormats` for the Camera popup's camera, read off the
151	    /// device now, and the stored format (`""` is Best).
152	    func rebuildCameraFormats() {
153	        let stored = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: Self.cameraFormatKey) ?? ""
154	        fillCameraFormats(
155	            selectedCameraID.flatMap(CameraDevices.device(withID:)).map(CameraDevices.facts(of:)),
156	            stored: stored.isEmpty ? nil : stored)
157	    }
158	
159	    // MARK: - The locks
160	
161	    /// Called last by `syncControlsEnabled`: the Camera and Format popups
162	    /// are live only while idle with a camera wanted, the box only while
163	    /// idle with a screen source (CAM-11 (1), (3)); with Source Camera the
164	    /// screen-only controls and Rate are greyed, their values kept.
165	    func syncCameraControls() {
166	        cameraPopup.isEnabled = phase == .idle && cameraWanted
167	        formatPopup.isEnabled = phase == .idle && cameraWanted
168	        cameraBesideCheckbox.isEnabled = phase == .idle && screenSourceSelected
169	        guard cameraSelected else { return }
170	        let screenAndRate: [NSControl] = [
171	            systemAudioSwitch, showClicksSwitch, sizePopup, includeFrameJobCheckbox, ratePopup,
172	            recordShortcutsCheckbox,
173	            cursorPopup,
174	        ]
175	        for control in screenAndRate { control.isEnabled = false }
176	    }
177	
178	    // MARK: - The size note
179	
180	    /// `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` (CAM-3's pick, the
181	    /// rate written `%g`) for Best, `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen
182	    /// format` for a row the camera lists (CAM-6 (4)); "no camera connected"
183	    /// for nil or a camera with no format.
184	    static func cameraSizeNote(_ camera: CameraDeviceFacts?, format: String? = nil) -> String {
185	        guard let camera else { return "no camera connected" }
186	        if let format,
187	            let chosen = camera.formats.first(where: { CameraDevices.spelled($0) == format })
188	        {
189	            return CameraDevices.formatTitle(chosen) + " — the chosen format"
190	        }
191	        guard let index = CameraDevices.bestFormat(camera.formats, active: camera.activeFormat)
192	        else { return "no camera connected" }
193	        return CameraDevices.formatTitle(camera.formats[index]) + " — the camera's best format"
194	    }
195	
196	    /// The size note for the chosen camera and format, read off the device
197	    /// now.
198	    var selectedCameraSizeNote: String {
199	        Self.cameraSizeNote(
200	            selectedCameraID.flatMap(CameraDevices.device(withID:)).map(CameraDevices.facts(of:)),
201	            format: selectedCameraFormat)
202	    }
203	
204	    // MARK: - The press and the launch
205	
206	    /// Record with Source Camera: no camera refuses with a note; otherwise
207	    /// the Camera grant, then the Microphone grant, then the countdown.
208	    /// Screen Recording is neither read nor asked.
209	    func beginCameraIfGranted() {
210	        guard selectedCameraID != nil else {
211	            setNote(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence)
212	            return
213	        }
214	        floatAgain()
215	        guard checkCameraGrant(), checkMicrophoneGrant() else { return }
216	        setNote("")
217	        beginCountdown()
218	    }
219	
220	    /// The countdown's end for a camera: handed to the recorder, which
221	    /// adopts the capture the countdown prepared and answers once the
222	    /// picture can begin, under its own arm ceiling.
223	    func launchCamera(_ choice: RecordingChoice) {
224	        launched = true
225	        recorder.startCamera(
226	            choice: choice, mayAsk: true,
227	            onFinish: { [weak self] outcome in self?.recordingEnded(outcome) }
228	        ) { [weak self] error in
229	            guard let self else { return }
230	            if let error {
231	                self.startFailed(error)
232	                return
233	            }
234	            self.recordingDidStart()
235	        }
236	    }
237	}

15	/// The camera's live preview in the panel (camera-recording CR2b, spec §11
16	/// CAM-7) — `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s eleventh file, NEW rather than
17	/// cut, as `+Camera.swift` was: the rule that says what the well shows, and
18	/// the one sync that acts on it. The well is `CameraPreviewWell`, a grid row
19	/// of its own right under Format (`+Rows.swift`), shown only while a camera
20	/// is wanted: Source Camera, or "Record the camera too" beside a screen
21	/// source (spec §11 CAM-11 (4)).
22	///
23	/// **The step** (`cameraPreviewStep`, pure, first match wins): a panel not
24	/// visible or closing, or no camera wanted → off; a camera recording, or a
25	/// screen recording's camera beside it → its layer; the countdown or
26	/// starting → the prepared layer, never a build; any other phase, or a
27	/// busy recorder → blank; no camera → "No camera is connected."; the
28	/// Camera grant not authorized → a sentence; a prepared capture that
29	/// failed, or a build that threw → its sentence, never retried; else
30	/// prepare. The grant is read only at its own step, through
31	/// `grantDoors.cameraStatus`, so showing the panel never prompts and a
32	/// hidden panel reads nothing.
33	///
34	/// **The sync** runs at the end of `show()`, of every control change, of
35	/// `syncPhase()`, at the one-second tick while the panel is visible, and at
36	/// each device notification. Its first act applies a pending hot-plug
37	/// (`+Devices.swift`, CAM-8 (2)), so the step sees the new selection. It
38	/// keeps the row's visibility (refitting the window when it changes), lets
39	/// the prepared capture go when the well is off or shows a sentence while
40	/// everything is idle, stops a failed prepared capture once (not at every
41	/// tick, CAM-8 (6)), and otherwise hosts the layer the step names. The
42	/// capture is the recorder's (`ScreenRecorder+CameraPrepare.swift`): the
43	/// countdown's `prepareCamera` keeps it, the panel's start adopts it, and a
44	/// tool's start never does (CAM-7 (7)), so through a tool's recording the
45	/// well reads "The camera is recording."
46	extension RecorderPanelController {
47	    static let previewGrantSentence = "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera."
48	    static let previewRecordingSentence = "The camera is recording."
49	
50	    /// CAM-7 (3)'s rule. `grant` and `failure` are called only at their own
51	    /// steps.
52	    static func cameraPreviewStep(
53	        visible: Bool, cameraSource: Bool, phase: Phase, recorderIdle: Bool,
54	        recordingCamera: Bool, cameraChosen: Bool, grant: () -> AVAuthorizationStatus,
55	        failure: () -> String?
56	    ) -> CameraPreviewStep {
57	        guard visible, cameraSource else { return .off }
58	        if recordingCamera { return .recording }
59	        switch phase {
60	        case .countdown, .starting: return .prepared
61	        case .idle: break
62	        case .recording, .paused, .stopping, .landing: return .blank
63	        }
64	        guard recorderIdle else { return .blank }
65	        guard cameraChosen else { return .message(CameraDevices.noCameraSentence) }
66	        guard grant() == .authorized else { return .message(Self.previewGrantSentence) }
67	        if let failure = failure() { return .failed(failure) }
68	        return .prepare
69	    }
70	
71	    /// The well's grid row.
72	    var cameraPreviewRow: NSGridRow? {
73	        (cameraPreview.superview as? NSGridView)?.cell(for: cameraPreview)?.row
74	    }
75	
76	    /// For the chosen camera at its resolved format (CAM-6 (3)): the
77	    /// prepared capture's stop on its own, else its failed start, else a
78	    /// failed build's record; nil when there is none.
79	    var previewFailure: String? {
80	        guard let id = selectedCameraID, let device = CameraDevices.device(withID: id) else {
81	            return nil
82	        }
83	        let facts = CameraDevices.facts(of: device)
84	        guard
85	            let format = CameraDevices.chosenFormat(
86	                selectedCameraFormat, in: facts.formats, active: facts.activeFormat)
87	        else { return nil }
88	        if let prepared = recorder.preparedCamera, prepared.deviceID == id, prepared.format == format,
89	            let sentence = prepared.stoppedOnItsOwn ?? prepared.startError?.localizedDescription
90	        {
91	            return sentence
92	        }
93	        guard let failure = recorder.preparedCameraFailure, failure.deviceID == id,
94	            failure.format == format
95	        else { return nil }
96	        return failure.sentence
97	    }
98	
99	    /// A pending hot-plug applied (CAM-8 (2)), the row's visibility, then the
100	    /// step acted on (the type doc).
101	    func syncCameraPreview() {
102	        applyPendingDevices()
103	        let hidden = !cameraWanted
104	        if let row = cameraPreviewRow, row.isHidden != hidden {
105	            row.isHidden = hidden
106	            fitWindowToContent()
107	        }
108	        let step = Self.cameraPreviewStep(
109	            visible: window?.isVisible == true && !panelClosing, cameraSource: cameraWanted,
110	            phase: phase, recorderIdle: recorder.state == .idle,
111	            recordingCamera: recorder.cameraSession != nil || recorder.session?.cameraCapture != nil,
112	            cameraChosen: selectedCameraID != nil,
113	            grant: { Self.grantDoors.cameraStatus() }, failure: { self.previewFailure })
114	        switch step {
115	        case .off, .message:
116	            if phase == .idle, recorder.state == .idle { recorder.discardPreparedCamera() }
117	            if case .message(let sentence) = step {
118	                cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
119	            } else {
120	                cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
121	            }
122	        case .failed(let sentence):
123	            if let capture = recorder.preparedCamera?.capture, !capture.stopped { capture.stop() }
124	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
125	        case .prepare:
126	            recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
127	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
128	        case .prepared:
129	            hostPreview(recorder.preparedCamera?.capture.previewLayer, else: nil)
130	        case .recording:
131	            hostPreview(
132	                (recorder.cameraSession?.capture ?? recorder.session?.cameraCapture)?.previewLayer,
133	                else: Self.previewRecordingSentence)
134	        case .blank:
135	            cameraPreview.showMessage(nil)
136	        }
137	    }
138	
139	    /// `layer` in the well, else `sentence` (nil a blank well).
140	    private func hostPreview(_ layer: AVCaptureVideoPreviewLayer?, else sentence: String?) {
141	        if let layer {
142	            cameraPreview.show(layer)
143	        } else {
144	            cameraPreview.showMessage(sentence)
145	        }
146	    }
147	}

3	/// Pause and resume from the panel's side, the one door into a hidden
4	/// recording's controls, and the phases drawn (road map 3, R2c) —
5	/// `RecorderPanelController.swift`'s sixth file, NEW rather than cut for its
6	/// first two members: they are the whole of what the panel adds for a pause,
7	/// and `+Recording.swift` and the base file were both within a dozen lines
8	/// of the 400-line cap when R2 began. `syncPhase` and `refreshStatusLabel`
9	/// then MOVED here from the base file when the R2 review's fixes took it
10	/// over the cap — the base file's toll, paid along the line the footnote
11	/// draws: its `.paused` and `.stopping` arms are what the pause added, and
12	/// `syncPhase` is its one caller besides the tick.
13	///
14	/// **Neither pause member is reachable from the panel's own controls** but
15	/// in a voice-over, whose panel stays up with a Pause / Resume button
16	/// (`+VoiceOver.swift`). The panel is off screen for every other recording
17	/// (decision 7), so Pause Recording
18	/// and Resume Recording are rows of the status item's menu, which calls
19	/// these through the closures `recordingDidStart` hands it, and File ▸
20	/// Pause/Resume Recording (`AppDelegate+Recording.swift`), the second door,
21	/// which calls them for the panel's own recording (#98). The panel's
22	/// phase — `.recording ⇄ .paused` — follows the recorder's own `pause()` /
23	/// `resume()` (`ScreenRecorder+Pause.swift`), which are synchronous and
24	/// throw. The phase moves only AFTER the call returns
25	/// without throwing, so the panel never claims a state the recorder
26	/// refused: a pause that could not close the segment's file leaves the
27	/// recorder `.recording` and the panel with it, and a resume whose output
28	/// could not be added leaves both `.paused`.
29	///
30	/// **The two refusals are answered differently, on purpose.** A refused
31	/// pause BEEPS: the recorder is still recording, nothing was lost, and the
32	/// panel is hidden, so a note there would be read by nobody until the
33	/// landing, by which time it would be stale. A refused resume keeps the
34	/// recorder's sentence as `resumeProblem` and stays paused: the stream still
35	/// captures but no file is taking it, so what the person does next — try
36	/// again, or stop and land what was recorded — depends on the sentence, and
37	/// the landing's reveal (`revealIfNoted`, `+Landing.swift`) brings the
38	/// panel back with that sentence in its note when they stop. The sentence
39	/// is STATE and never text read back off the label (R2 review): the live
40	/// note is rebuilt from `[microphoneProblem, resumeProblem]` at every tick
41	/// (`syncMicrophoneNote`, over `liveNote` below), so a microphone
42	/// did-finish landing late cannot wipe it and a retried resume replaces it
43	/// rather than appending a second copy; and `landingNote` takes it as an
44	/// argument, so the landing's note carries it where the first shape — each
45	/// end replacing the label whole — dropped it, and the reveal showed
46	/// nothing. A resume that LANDS clears it: a sentence about a refusal the
47	/// person has since got past would bring the panel back with nothing true
48	/// to say.
49	///
50	/// A Stop while paused (`stopRecording`, `record(_:)`, File ▸ Stop
51	/// Recording) goes to `recorder.stop()` exactly as one while recording
52	/// does — the recorder's `.paused` arm takes the same finishing path with
53	/// the segment's output already closed — and the status item comes down at
54	/// `recordingEnded` as ever. The tick runs through `.paused` (`armTick`):
55	/// the meter poll is a no-op there, the recorder having silenced the bar at
56	/// the pause, and `elapsed` is frozen, so the footnote and the item hold
57	/// still on their own.
58	extension RecorderPanelController {
59	    // MARK: - Pause and resume
60	
61	    /// The status item's Pause Recording, and File ▸ Pause Recording's for
62	    /// the panel's own recording. `.recording` → `.paused`; any
63	    /// other phase beeps — the row was clicked in the moment between a Stop
64	    /// and the item coming down — and so does any throw, `.alreadyPaused`
65	    /// among them (the header).
66	    func pauseRecording() {
67	        guard phase == .recording else {
68	            NSSound.beep()
69	            return
70	        }
71	        do {
72	            try recorder.pause()
73	            phase = .paused
74	        } catch {
75	            NSSound.beep()
76	        }
77	    }
78	
79	    /// The status item's Resume Recording, and File ▸ Resume Recording's.
80	    /// `.paused` → `.recording`, with
81	    /// the refused-resume sentence cleared; any other phase beeps. A throw
82	    /// leaves the phase paused and keeps the recorder's sentence as
83	    /// `resumeProblem`, REPLACING an earlier one, redrawn into the note at
84	    /// once rather than at the tick's next turn (the header).
85	    func resumeRecording() {
86	        guard phase == .paused else {
87	            NSSound.beep()
88	            return
89	        }
90	        do {
91	            try recorder.resume()
92	            resumeProblem = nil
93	            phase = .recording
94	        } catch {
95	            resumeProblem = error.localizedDescription
96	            syncMicrophoneNote()
97	        }
98	    }
99	
100	    /// The live note's two parts, in order: the microphone's sentence, with
101	    /// the fact that the picture is still recording (a silent meter alone
102	    /// reads as a broken recording), then a refused resume's; empty with
103	    /// neither. Pure, so a probe can pin the composition without a recorder.
104	    static func liveNote(microphoneProblem: String?, resumeProblem: String?) -> String {
105	        var sentences: [String] = []
106	        if let microphoneProblem {
107	            sentences.append(
108	                "The microphone stopped: \(microphoneProblem) The picture is still recording.")
109	        }
110	        if let resumeProblem { sentences.append(resumeProblem) }
111	        return sentences.joined(separator: " ")
112	    }
113	
114	    // MARK: - The hidden recording's one door
115	
116	    /// The quit guard's call (`AppDelegate.applicationShouldTerminate`).
117	    /// While this panel is hidden for its recording `show()` can only beep,
118	    /// and a beep tells a person who paused and forgot nothing — so the
119	    /// status item's menu is opened instead, Pause or Resume and Stop put
120	    /// in front of them (`RecorderStatusItem.openMenu`); the beep is kept
121	    /// for the one case with no item to open. Any other recording — a
122	    /// tool's, which File ▸ Stop Recording ends — shows the panel as before.
123	    func revealControls() {
124	        guard hiddenForRecording else {
125	            show()
126	            return
127	        }
128	        if statusItem?.openMenu() != true { NSSound.beep() }
129	    }
130	
131	    // MARK: - The phases, drawn
132	
133	    /// Draws the phase: the button's title and enabled state, the controls
134	    /// locked while anything is in flight, the countdown numeral, the
135	    /// footnote, the camera preview (CAM-7), and the window refitted to
136	    /// whatever appeared or went.
137	    func syncPhase() {
138	        syncControlsEnabled()
139	        syncPauseButton()
140	        var countdown: String?
141	        switch phase {
142	        case .idle:
143	            recordButton.title = "Record"
144	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
145	        case .countdown(let remaining):
146	            recordButton.title = "Cancel"
147	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
148	            countdown = "\(remaining)"
149	        case .starting:
150	            recordButton.title = "Starting…"
151	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
152	        case .recording, .paused:
153	            recordButton.title = "Stop"
154	            recordButton.isEnabled = true
155	        case .stopping:
156	            recordButton.title = "Stopping…"
157	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
158	        case .landing:
159	            recordButton.title = "Adding…"
160	            recordButton.isEnabled = false
161	        }
162	        recordButton.invalidateIntrinsicContentSize()
163	        countdownLabel.stringValue = countdown ?? ""
164	        countdownLabel.isHidden = countdown == nil
165	        refreshStatusLabel()
166	        syncCameraPreview()
167	        fitWindowToContent()
168	    }
169	
170	    /// The footnote: the folder while idle, the coral dot and the elapsed
171	    /// time while recording, the pause glyph and the frozen time while
172	    /// paused — faint, because the dot's colour means "capturing" — and
173	    /// through `.stopping` whichever of those two it last showed, left
174	    /// UNTOUCHED (R2 review): the phase no longer says whether the Stop
175	    /// came from paused, `elapsed` is frozen at the stop call, and
176	    /// redrawing the arm as recording brought the coral dot back over a
177	    /// finish that captures nothing. The status item keeps its mark the
178	    /// same way (`RecorderStatusItem.freeze`, called by `stopRecording`).
179	    func refreshStatusLabel() {
180	        switch phase {
181	        case .recording:
182	            statusLabel.stringValue = "● " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
183	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.meterClip
184	        case .paused:
185	            statusLabel.stringValue =
186	                RecorderStatusItem.pauseGlyph + " " + RecorderStatusItem.label(for: recorder.elapsed)
187	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
188	        case .stopping:
189	            break
190	        default:
191	            statusLabel.stringValue =
192	                "saved in " + (RecordingFiles.folder().path as NSString).abbreviatingWithTildeInPath
193	            statusLabel.textColor = DS.textFaint
194	        }
195	    }

48	/// **The microphone is prepared at the countdown's start** (R1 review;

141	    /// 3, 2, 1 in the panel, one second each — `TimelineView.flashRefusal`'s

144	    /// meanwhile, and a click on it or closing the panel ends the countdown

146	    /// here, after the grants and before the first second has passed, so its

150	    /// first, so its sentence does not carry into this one's note (#193).

153	        resumeProblem = nil
154	        phase = .countdown(Self.countdownSeconds)
155	        recorder.prepareCamera(for: currentChoice())
156	        recorder.prepareMicrophone(currentChoice().microphone)
157	        armTick()
158	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
159	            guard let self, case .countdown(let remaining) = self.phase else {
160	                timer.invalidate()

162	            }
163	            if remaining > 1 {
164	                self.phase = .countdown(remaining - 1)
165	            } else {
166	                timer.invalidate()

185	    /// The choice as the controls stand, then the filter: a picked window's
186	    /// is the picker's own; a display's is built from the shareable content
187	    /// and leaves out what `recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows:)`
188	    /// names (`ScreenRecorder.filter(for:in:excluding:)`) — Frame Job's own
189	    /// application, which keeps the document windows out of a display
190	    /// recording's picture, or with Include Frame Job windows on the panel's
191	    /// window alone. One attempt, numbered and bounded (the type doc).
192	    private func startRecording() {
193	        let choice = currentChoice()
194	        let exclusion = recordingExclusion(includeFrameJobWindows: choice.includeFrameJobWindows)
195	        startGeneration += 1
196	        let generation = startGeneration
197	        launched = false
198	        phase = .starting
199	        // A voice-over has no lookup to bound (`+VoiceOver.swift`).
200	        if choice.source == .voiceOver { return launchVoiceOver(choice) }
201	        // Nor does a camera: the recorder's own arm ceiling bounds it.
202	        if choice.source == .camera { return launchCamera(choice) }
203	        startTimer?.invalidate()
204	        startTimer = Timer.scheduledTimer(
205	            withTimeInterval: ScreenRecorder.armCeiling, repeats: false
206	        ) { [weak self] _ in self?.armTimedOut(generation: generation) }
207	        if choice.source == .picked, let filter = pickedFilter {
208	            launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
209	            return
210	        }
211	        ScreenRecorder.shareableContent { [weak self] outcome in
212	            guard let self, self.phase == .starting, generation == self.startGeneration else {
213	                return
214	            }
215	            switch outcome {
216	            case .failure(let error):
217	                self.startFailed(error)
218	            case .success(let content):
219	                do {
220	                    let filter = try ScreenRecorder.filter(
221	                        for: choice.source, in: content, excluding: exclusion)
222	                    self.launch(filter: filter, choice: choice)
223	                } catch {
224	                    self.startFailed(error)
225	                }
226	            }
227	        }
228	    }

230	    /// The arm ceiling, for the lookup half of an attempt: a stale number, a
231	    /// phase that moved on, or an attempt the recorder already holds (its
232	    /// own ceiling reports that one) does nothing. Internal so a probe can
233	    /// fire it without a lookup.
234	    func armTimedOut(generation: Int) {
235	        guard phase == .starting, generation == startGeneration, !launched else { return }
236	        startFailed(RecorderError.startTimedOut)
237	    }

239	    /// A Stop before the recorder was handed the attempt: the pending
240	    /// lookup's answer is orphaned by the generation bump, the prepared
241	    /// microphone let go, and the panel idle with a note saying nothing was
242	    /// recorded.
243	    private func abandonStart() {
244	        startGeneration += 1

317	    /// 30 Hz from the countdown's start, in `.common` modes (the type doc).
318	    /// Through `.countdown` and `.starting` it ONLY meters — the prepared
319	    /// session's level (#98 c; the recorder publishes nothing while
320	    /// arming, so the bar holds its last pre-roll level for that instant).
321	    /// While recording or paused: the microphone's level into the panel's
322	    /// own meter (`ScreenRecorder.publishMicrophoneLevel`, a no-op without
323	    /// a microphone and while paused, the recorder having silenced the
324	    /// bar), the elapsed time in the footnote and in the status item — with
325	    /// `paused`, which is what flips the item's menu — and a microphone
326	    /// problem into the note. `recordingDidStart` re-arms it.
327	    private func armTick() {
328	        tickTimer?.invalidate()
329	        let timer = Timer(timeInterval: 1.0 / 30, repeats: true) { [weak self] timer in
330	            guard let self else {
331	                timer.invalidate()
332	                return
333	            }
334	            switch self.phase {
335	            case .countdown, .starting:
336	                self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
337	                return
338	            default:
339	                break
340	            }
341	            guard self.phase == .recording || self.phase == .paused || self.phase == .stopping
342	            else {
343	                timer.invalidate()
344	                return
345	            }
346	            self.recorder.publishMicrophoneLevel()
347	            self.refreshStatusLabel()
348	            self.statusItem?.update(elapsed: self.recorder.elapsed, paused: self.phase == .paused)
349	            self.syncMicrophoneNote()
350	        }
351	        RunLoop.main.add(timer, forMode: .common)
352	        tickTimer = timer
353	    }

155	/// Decision 2 (road map 3 §0): a recording is ORIGINAL footage and lives in
156	/// `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/`, named by date and time — never in the
157	/// package (an untitled document has none) and never in the temporary
158	/// directory (where a cache is regenerable and footage would be lost). The
159	/// folder is created on demand, and `-RCRecordingFolder` overrides it the
160	/// way `-RCFFmpegPath` overrides the binary (`FFmpegRewrap.locate`), so a
161	/// proof can record into `tools/proof/work/` and delete it.
162	enum RecordingFiles {
163	    /// The launch-argument override, read from `UserDefaults.standard` so it
164	    /// works from the argument domain (`-RCRecordingFolder ~/x` on the
165	    /// command line, or a pinned volatile domain in a probe).
166	    static let folderDefaultsKey = "RCRecordingFolder"
167	
168	    /// The default folder's name under `~/Movies`.
169	    static let folderName = "Frame Job Recordings"
170	
171	    /// The folder a recording goes into: the override, tilde-expanded, when
172	    /// one is set; `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings/` otherwise. Nothing is
173	    /// created here — `create(_:)` is called at the moment a recording has
174	    /// something to put in it, `AppSupport`'s rule.
175	    static func folder() -> URL {
176	        if let override = UserDefaults.standard.string(forKey: folderDefaultsKey),
177	            !override.isEmpty
178	        {
179	            return URL(
180	                fileURLWithPath: (override as NSString).expandingTildeInPath, isDirectory: true)
181	        }
182	        let movies =
183	            FileManager.default.urls(for: .moviesDirectory, in: .userDomainMask).first
184	            ?? FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser.appendingPathComponent(
185	                "Movies", isDirectory: true)
186	        return movies.appendingPathComponent(folderName, isDirectory: true)
187	    }

189	    /// `Screen Recording 2026-09-10 at 14.03.22` — the Screenshot app's
190	    /// spelling, in the machine's own time zone. The formatter is pinned to
191	    /// `en_US_POSIX` so a locale with another digit set or a 12-hour clock
192	    /// cannot change the name's shape; the seconds make a name unique across
193	    /// the app's own recordings and `uniqueURL` handles the rest.
194	    static func stem(at date: Date) -> String {
195	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
196	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
197	        formatter.timeZone = .current
198	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Screen Recording' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
199	        return formatter.string(from: date)
200	    }
201	
202	    /// `Voice-over 2026-10-02 at 09.15.04` — a voice-over's file, `stem(at:)`'s
203	    /// spelling and pinning with its own lead word.
204	    static func voiceOverStem(at date: Date) -> String {
205	        let formatter = DateFormatter()
206	        formatter.locale = Locale(identifier: "en_US_POSIX")
207	        formatter.timeZone = .current
208	        formatter.dateFormat = "'Voice-over' yyyy-MM-dd 'at' HH.mm.ss"
209	        return formatter.string(from: date)
210	    }

212	    /// `<stem>.<ext>` in `folder`, or `<stem> (2).<ext>`, `<stem> (3).<ext>`…
213	    /// while a file of that name exists — the Finder's own collision rule.
214	    static func uniqueURL(in folder: URL, stem: String, ext: String) -> URL {
215	        let manager = FileManager.default
216	        var candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent(stem).appendingPathExtension(ext)
217	        var counter = 2
218	        while manager.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) {
219	            candidate = folder.appendingPathComponent("\(stem) (\(counter))")
220	                .appendingPathExtension(ext)
221	            counter += 1
222	        }
223	        return candidate
224	    }

226	    /// The microphone's own file, beside the movie: the movie's stem plus
227	    /// ` (Microphone)`, as `.m4a` (R0 q6b: `AVCaptureAudioFileOutput` writes
228	    /// one mono 48 kHz AAC track there), made unique the same way.
229	    static func microphoneURL(beside movie: URL) -> URL {
230	        let stem = movie.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent + " (Microphone)"
231	        return uniqueURL(in: movie.deletingLastPathComponent(), stem: stem, ext: "m4a")
232	    }

234	    /// Makes the folder, intermediate directories included. A folder that

238	            at: folder, withIntermediateDirectories: true)
239	    }

244	/// The two ScreenCaptureKit configurations a choice becomes. PURE — every
245	/// field is set from the arguments and read back by the probe — which is
246	/// what lets the `excludesCurrentProcessAudio` mutant be caught at all: it
247	/// is invisible over MCP (nothing plays during a headless recording) and
248	/// this is the only row that sees it.
249	enum RecordingConfiguration {
250	    /// System audio is asked for at 48 kHz stereo, the rate the tap and
251	    /// `Loudness.swift` already assume of every file.
252	    static let sampleRate = 48_000
253	    static let channelCount = 2
254	
255	    /// `displayPointSize` and `scale` come from the caller, and the caller is
256	    /// `ScreenRecorder.start`, which reads them off the FILTER — its
257	    /// `contentRect` (points) and `pointPixelScale` — the one geometry
258	    /// source that also covers a picker-made filter (`SCDisplay`'s
259	    /// `width`/`height` are POINTS, R0 q4, and a display filter reports the
260	    /// display's point size and backing scale, a window filter the window's
261	    /// frame). The probe passes the numbers directly. `outputURL` is
262	    /// assigned before the output configuration is returned, and must stay
263	    /// so: reading `outputURL` off a fresh `SCRecordingOutputConfiguration`
264	    /// TRAPS (it imports non-optional and is nil underneath until assigned —
265	    /// the SDK scout's finding, exit 133).
266	    static func make(
267	        _ choice: RecordingChoice, displayPointSize: CGSize, scale: CGFloat, outputURL: URL
268	    ) -> (stream: SCStreamConfiguration, output: SCRecordingOutputConfiguration) {
269	        let stream = SCStreamConfiguration()
270	        // R0 q4: pixels are asked for, `.best` does not scale by itself.
271	        let factor: CGFloat = choice.resolution == .best ? max(scale, 1) : 1
272	        stream.width = Int((displayPointSize.width * factor).rounded())
273	        stream.height = Int((displayPointSize.height * factor).rounded())
274	        stream.captureResolution = choice.resolution == .best ? .best : .nominal
275	        stream.minimumFrameInterval = CMTime(value: 1, timescale: CMTimeScale(max(choice.rate, 1)))
276	        // CU-31: the pointer and its ring are the stream's only In the picture.
277	        let inPicture = choice.effectiveCursor == .inPicture
278	        stream.showsCursor = inPicture
279	        stream.showMouseClicks = choice.showClicks && inPicture
280	        // R0 q6a: the click circle draws only under BGRA; the default `420v`
281	        // is left alone when the stream draws no clicks, so an ordinary
282	        // recording's pixel path is byte for byte the spike's.
283	        if choice.showClicks && inPicture { stream.pixelFormat = REDACTED }
284	        stream.capturesAudio = choice.systemAudio
285	        stream.sampleRate = sampleRate
286	        stream.channelCount = channelCount
287	        // ALWAYS: the timeline can play while a recording runs and must not
288	        // be in it. `captureMicrophone` is deliberately never touched (R0
289	        // q2 — the microphone is a second file), so it keeps its default of
290	        // false, which the probe reads back on every row.
291	        stream.excludesCurrentProcessAudio = true
292	
293	        let output = SCRecordingOutputConfiguration()
294	        output.outputURL = outputURL
295	        output.outputFileType = .mov
296	        // R0 q2: `availableVideoCodecTypes` is `[avc1, hvc1]` here and the
297	        // default is `avc1`; HEVC halves the file where the encoder offers it.
298	        output.videoCodecType =
299	            output.availableVideoCodecTypes.contains(.hevc) ? .hevc : .h264
300	        return (stream, output)
301	    }
302	}

3	/// CAM-3's warm-up rule and the type of its facts (camera-recording CR2-0,
4	/// spec §11 CAM-3): the run, the tolerance and the bound, `isSteady`, and
5	/// `WarmUp` with its `note`, moved out of `CameraCapture.swift` at the
6	/// 400-line cap as a pure move. The warm-up's running state (`Warming`,
7	/// `warmUpBuffer`, `endWarmUp`) stays in `CameraCapture.swift`, because it
8	/// is private stored state.
9	extension CameraCapture {
10	    /// CAM-3's warm-up: five intervals in a row within 15 % of the frame
11	    /// duration (a cold interval is 30 % long; the spike's steady stream
12	    /// never passed 5 %), bounded at 1 s.
13	    static let warmUpRun = 5
14	    static let warmUpTolerance = 0.15
15	    static let warmUpBound: TimeInterval = 1.0
16	
17	    /// What the warm-up waited for: its length from the session's start,
18	    /// the buffers seen, whether the stream reached the format's rate, the
19	    /// rate it ran at over the buffers seen, and their intervals in ms.
20	    struct WarmUp: Equatable {
21	        let seconds: Double
22	        let buffers: Int
23	        let steady: Bool
24	        let rate: Double
25	        let wanted: Double
26	        let intervals: [Double]
27	
28	        /// The result's `camera.note` when the bound passed first; nil when
29	        /// the stream was steady.
30	        var note: String? {
31	            guard !steady else { return nil }
32	            let bound = String(format: "%g", CameraCapture.warmUpBound)
33	            guard rate > 0 else {
34	                return "The camera delivered no steady frames in the \(bound) s it was given to "
35	                    + "settle; the recording began anyway."
36	            }
37	            return String(format: "The camera ran at %.1f fps, not its %g, ", rate, wanted)
38	                + "in the \(bound) s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway."
39	        }
40	    }
41	
42	    /// Whether one frame interval is on the format's rate (CAM-3).
43	    static func isSteady(_ interval: Double, frame: Double) -> Bool {
44	        abs(interval - frame) <= frame * warmUpTolerance
45	    }

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — with its `ReelCore+<Area>.swift` files, the only files
  that call `rc_*` (spec §11 CJ-8 (l)); a new wrapper goes in the file of its
  area. `ReelCore.swift` holds `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25) and `ReelAgentSocket` (below);
  `ReelCore+MediaFiles.swift` holds the media files the core reads or writes —
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index, #216-R), `ReelCube`,
  `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`, `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18;

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.
