---
title: The recorder panel
description: Set up a recording in the New Recording panel, from what to record and where it lands to what each control does and what the panel remembers.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The New Recording panel holds every recording choice in one place: record a display, a window, a camera or the microphone, straight into a project.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording… on the Welcome window"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The macOS permission for what you record, asked for when you press Record."
/>

## Open the panel

Choose **File ▸ New Recording…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>, or click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). You don't need a project open, and the menu item is always available.

There's one panel for the whole app. A recording doesn't belong to a project window, so it carries on if you close one.

While a recording runs, paused included, the same menu item reads **File ▸ Stop Recording** and <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> stops the recording. The Welcome window's button never stops one: during a screen recording it beeps, and during a camera recording or a voice-over it shows the panel again.

<Shot
  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
  alt="The New Recording panel. From the top: Source set to Built-in Retina Display, the Include Frame Job windows and Record the camera too boxes, greyed Camera, Format and Layout rows, Microphone set to Off with a level meter, System Audio on, Cursor set to Separate, Show Clicks off, the Record shortcuts box, the When it lands boxes with Zoom in on clicks ticked, Rate at 60 fps, Size at Nominal (points) with a note reading 2056×1329 points, 4112×2658 pixels, and Record Into set to a project. Saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings sits at the bottom left, beside Close and Record."
/>

## Make a recording

<Steps>

1. Choose what to record in [**Source**](#choose-a-source).

2. Choose where it goes in [**Record Into**](#choose-where-it-lands).

3. Set any other [controls](#the-controls). Rows that don't apply to your source are greyed out.

4. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) that source needs, then counts down from 3.

5. Stop when you're done. See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/).

</Steps>

**Close** closes the panel without recording.

A recording is saved as an ordinary movie or audio file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, then imported like any other media, so every edit, effect and export works on it. It [lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) at the playhead of the project you chose, or opens as a new project.

## Choose a source

**Source** lists one row for each connected display, by name, and then three more.

| Row | What it records |
| --- | --- |
| A display's name | [The whole display](/recording/record-a-display/). |
| **Window…** | [One window](/recording/record-a-window/), which you pick with macOS's window picker. |
| **Camera** | [A camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/), with no screen. |
| **Microphone Only** | [A voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/): the microphone with no picture. |

It starts on the display you used last, or the main display if there isn't one. Every display is listed even before Frame Job has the Screen Recording permission, so the panel can open and tell you what's missing.

To record a camera as well as the screen, keep a display or **Window…** as the source and tick **Record the camera too**. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).

## Choose where it lands

**Record Into** lists **New Project** first, then every open project by name. It starts on the project in front, or **New Project** when none is open.

The row follows whichever project is in front until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open, and if you close the project it goes back to following the one in front. If you choose **New Project**, it stays there.

The list updates every second while the panel is idle. From the press of **Record** to the landing it's frozen, so clicking into another project during a recording doesn't change where the recording goes.

**Record Into** is never remembered between launches.

## The controls

These are the panel's rows in order, with what each starts on before you've changed anything.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Source** | [What to record](#choose-a-source). | The main display |
| **Include Frame Job windows** | [Puts Frame Job's own windows](/recording/record-a-display/#include-frame-job-windows) into a display recording and into the window picker's list. | Off |
| **Record the camera too** | [Records a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/). | Off |
| **Camera** | [Which camera to record](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-camera). | The Mac's preferred camera |
| **Format** | [The camera's size and frame rate](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-format). | Best |
| **Preview** | [A live picture of the camera](/recording/record-a-camera/#check-the-picture). This row appears only when a camera is wanted. | |
| **Layout** | [Where the camera lands](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) beside the screen. | Corner |
| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | [Cuts the person out](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) of the camera's clips. | Off |
| **Microphone** | [**Off**, or a connected microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/), with a level meter beside it. | Off |
| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | [Runs Enhance Voice](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the microphone's clips. | Off |
| **System Audio** | [Records what the Mac plays](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/). | On |
| **Cursor** | [Whether the pointer is drawn into the movie](/recording/cursor/): **Separate** or **In the picture**. | Separate |
| **Show Clicks** | [Marks each mouse click](/recording/cursor/). | Off |
| **Record shortcuts** | [Records the shortcuts you press](/recording/record-shortcuts/), and when you type, but never what you type. | Off |
| **When it lands:** **Zoom in on clicks** | [Runs Auto Zoom](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the screen clips. | On |
| **Show shortcuts** | [Adds shortcut overlays](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | On |
| **Speed up typing** | [Runs Speed Up Typing](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | Off |
| **Rate** | [The most frames per second](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) the file may hold, and a new project's frame rate. | 60 fps |
| **Size** | [Records at points or pixels](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size). | Nominal (points) |
| **Record Into** | [Where the recording lands](#choose-where-it-lands). | The project in front, else New Project |

## What greys out

Rows that don't apply to the chosen source grey out and keep their values, so nothing jumps and your settings are still there when you switch back.

| When | Greyed out |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** is **Microphone Only** | **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout**, the background box, **System Audio**, **Cursor**, **Show Clicks**, **Record shortcuts**, the three **When it lands:** boxes and **Size**. **Rate** stays live, because it sets a new project's frame rate. |
| **Source** is **Camera** | The same rows, except **Camera** and **Format**, which go live. **Rate** greys out as well, because a camera records at its format's rate. |
| **Record the camera too** is off, with a display or window | **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and the background box. |
| **Microphone** is **Off** | **Enhance the microphone when it lands**. |
| **Record shortcuts** is off | **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. |

**Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live for every source.

Every control locks from the press of **Record** until the recording has landed.

## The note under Size

A line under **Size** tells you what you'll get from the chosen source.

| Source | The note reads |
| --- | --- |
| A display | Both its sizes, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels` |
| A picked window | "the picked window's own size" |
| **Microphone Only** | "no picture — the microphone alone" |
| **Camera**, with **Format** on Best | For example `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` |
| **Camera**, with a format chosen | For example `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen format` |
| **Camera**, with none connected | "no camera connected" |

## The footnote

The text at the bottom left of the panel shows where recordings are saved, for example `saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`.

When the panel stays up during a recording, as it does for a camera or a voice-over, the footnote shows the time instead: the coral **●** and the elapsed time while recording, or **❚❚** and the time held still while paused.

## What the panel remembers

The panel reopens as you left it, between launches. It keeps:

- the display, the microphone, the camera and the camera format
- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks** and **Cursor**
- **Rate** and **Size**
- every box: **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and the three **When it lands:** boxes
- **Layout**

A few things work differently:

- **Cursor** is remembered only once you choose it. Until then it shows Separate, and a choice you make holds for every source.
- The camera format is one choice for every camera. A camera that doesn't have it shows Best.
- A picked window, and **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the **Source** row, last until you quit. The camera itself is remembered.
- **Record Into** isn't remembered.

A display that's no longer connected falls back to the main display, a microphone to **Off**, and a camera to the default camera.

## Keys in the panel

<kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Record** and <kbd>Esc</kbd> presses **Close**.

Those two buttons change as a recording goes on, and the keys go with them. During the countdown <kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Cancel**, and while a camera or a voice-over records it presses **Stop**. <kbd>Esc</kbd> always closes the panel, which ends a countdown but leaves a running recording going.

The panel takes the keyboard only when you open it with Frame Job active. Opened while another app is in front, it leaves the keyboard with that app, so <kbd>Return</kbd> goes there.

## How the panel floats

The panel is built to sit beside whatever you're about to record.

- It stays above other windows, and it doesn't hide when you switch to another app.
- Clicking it doesn't make Frame Job the active app, so your project windows don't jump over the app you're recording.
- Opened while Frame Job is in the background, it comes to the front without taking the keyboard, so your typing stays where it was.
- It opens in the centre of the screen. Drag it anywhere, and it stays there until you quit.
- It pushes itself back onto its display when the countdown or a note makes it taller, so **Cancel** never ends up under the Dock. Its top-left corner stays put unless the screen edge forces a move.

For a display or a window, the panel [leaves the screen](/recording/record-a-display/#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record) once the recording starts.

## With an agent

An agent doesn't use the panel. `record_screen` records for a set time, from 1 to 600 seconds, with no panel and no countdown, and answers once the recording has landed.

- The recording lands at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, nest included, or on a new track in front when that one has no room. With no project open, it opens as a new untitled project.
- The tool never asks for a permission and never opens the window picker. A missing permission is refused by name, with the System Settings pane to go to, so grant it once from the panel. A Frame Job launched from a terminal runs under the terminal's permissions.
- The [assistant](/assistant/overview/) can't call it.

[Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/) has every argument, and the order its refusals come in.

## Related

- [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/)
- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)

---
title: Record a display
description: Record everything on one display, choose its size and frame rate, and decide whether Frame Job's own windows appear in the picture.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a display when you want everything on one screen in the movie: a demo that moves between apps, or a tutorial with menus and dialogs.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording permission."
/>

## Record a display

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

2. Choose the display by name in **Source**. There's one row for each connected display, and the panel starts on the display you used last, or the main display.

3. Set [**Size**](#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](#choose-a-frame-rate), and anything else you want, such as the [microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).

4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown the panel [leaves the screen](#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record) and recording starts.

5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

</Steps>

The recording lands in the project you chose in **Record Into**. See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/).

## Choose a size

**Size** sets how many pixels the movie holds.

| Size | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Nominal (points)** | The display's point size. This is the default. |
| **Best (pixels)** | Every pixel: the point size times the display's scale, which is twice the points on a Retina display. |

The note under the row shows both for the chosen display, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels`.

Choose **Best (pixels)** when small text has to stay sharp, and **Nominal (points)** for smaller files. An odd width or height is rounded up to an even number when the movie is encoded.

## Choose a frame rate

**Rate** is **30 fps** or **60 fps**, and starts on 60 fps. It does two things:

- It's the most frames per second the file may hold.
- It's the frame rate of a new project made from the recording.

It's a ceiling, not a promise. macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That's the file doing its job and not a fault.

**Rate** greys out for **Camera**, which records at its format's rate. It stays live for **Microphone Only**, where it sets a new project's frame rate.

## Include Frame Job windows

---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a window when only one app matters. The movie is that window alone, at its own size, with nothing else on your screen in it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Window…"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording permission."
/>

## Record a window

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

2. Choose **Window…** in **Source**. macOS's window picker opens.

3. Click the window you want. **Source** now reads **Window (picked)**, and the note under **Size** reads "the picked window's own size".

4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown the panel leaves the screen and recording starts.

5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

</Steps>

[**Size**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) work as they do for a display: **Nominal (points)** records the window at its point size, and **Best (pixels)** at every pixel.

If the window closes while you're recording, see [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).

## Pick a different window

Choose **Window (picked)** again to open the picker and pick another window.

Choosing any other row in **Source** drops the pick. A pick lasts until you quit: close and reopen the panel and it's still there, but it's never remembered between launches.

## If you cancel the picker

Cancel the picker and **Source** goes back to the display you used last, or the main display. That's also true when you've already picked a window and choose the row again, so the earlier pick is gone.

If the picker can't open at all, **Source** goes back the same way and the panel reads "The window picker could not open: …" with the reason.

## Which windows the picker lists

The picker lists other apps' windows. Frame Job's own windows depend on **Include Frame Job windows**:

| Box | The picker lists |
| --- | --- |
| Off | None of Frame Job's windows |
| On | Frame Job's windows, but never the recorder panel |

The box only changes the next time the picker opens. A window you've already picked stays picked.

## Record needs a picked window

If you press **Record** while the row still reads **Window…**, with nothing picked, the panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display." No countdown starts, so nothing wrong gets recorded.

## With an agent

An agent doesn't use the picker. It names a window by its system window id, and an id that doesn't name a window Frame Job can record is refused. It can't name a window and a display at once. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).

---
title: Record a camera
description: Record a connected camera on its own, with no screen, and choose its format, check its picture and see where the movie lands.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a camera on its own when you want a piece to camera with no screen in it. Frame Job records the chosen camera at the chosen format's highest frame rate.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Camera"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Camera permission, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone. Screen Recording isn't needed."
/>

## Record a camera on its own

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> and choose **Camera** in **Source**.

2. Choose the camera in [**Camera**](#choose-a-camera) and its size and frame rate in [**Format**](#choose-a-format).

3. Check the live picture in the [**Preview**](#check-the-picture) under **Format**.

4. Choose a microphone in **Microphone**, or leave it **Off** to record the camera alone. The microphone can be the camera's own, if macOS lists it, and it's recorded to its own file beside the movie.

5. Choose where it goes in **Record Into**.

6. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown recording starts, and the panel [stays up](#stop-and-pause-from-the-panel).

</Steps>

With no camera connected, pressing **Record** says "No camera is connected."

**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Rate** and the other rows for the screen grey out, and keep their values for next time. **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live.

To record a camera and the screen at once, see [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).

## Choose a camera

**Camera** lists each connected camera by name, or a single row, **None connected**, when there isn't one. An iPhone used as a Continuity Camera has "(Continuity Camera)" after its name.

It starts on the camera you used last, then the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected.

The row is live when **Source** is **Camera** or **Record the camera too** is ticked, and greyed out otherwise.

## Choose a format

**Format** sets the size and frame rate the camera records at.

**Best** comes first and names what it will pick, for example **Best (1760×1328 at 30 fps)**. The camera's other formats follow, written like **1920×1080 at 30 fps**. Sizes wider than tall come first, then square, then taller than wide, each largest first.

Each format records at its highest frame rate, so you can't choose a lower rate within a format's range.

It starts on the format you used last when the chosen camera has it, otherwise **Best**. The row is live and greyed out at the same times as **Camera**.

## What Best picks

**Best** is the largest format wider than tall that reaches 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate. If two formats are the same size, the higher rate wins, and then the one the camera lists first.

If no format wider than tall reaches 30 fps, Frame Job looks at every shape the same way. If none of those does either, it uses the format the camera is already set to.

## Check the picture

The **Preview** under **Format** shows the chosen camera live at the chosen format, as the movie will record it. It isn't mirrored, so you see what's being filmed, and the whole picture is fitted inside the well.

The row appears only when **Source** is **Camera** or **Record the camera too** is ticked, and it stays live through the countdown and the recording.

Sometimes it shows words instead of a picture.

| The preview reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | Frame Job doesn't have the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does. |
| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording the camera. The picture comes back when it's done. |
| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. To try again, choose another source and then **Camera**, or close and reopen the panel. |

## How the camera warms up

The camera starts as soon as the panel shows it, so it's ready before you record, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing another source turns it off, unless **Record the camera too** is ticked there, and so does closing the panel.

A camera that's starting cold can take a moment to run at its full rate. Frame Job gives it up to a second, in the countdown, so the recording starts steady, and then holds the camera to the chosen format and rate for the whole recording.

If it never settles, the recording begins anyway, and the note when it lands names the rate it ran at, for example "The camera ran at 24.3 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway."

## Stop and pause from the panel

The panel stays on screen while a camera records, because nothing on screen is being filmed.

- The controls lock and the microphone's level meter stays live.
- The [footnote](/recording/recorder-panel/#the-footnote) shows **●** or **❚❚** with the time.
- **Record** reads **Stop**, with a **Pause** or **Resume** button beside it.

Choose **Close** and the panel goes away, but the recording carries on under the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/). See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) for the other ways to stop.

## Where a camera recording lands

The movie is saved as `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, with any microphone in its own `.m4a` file beside it.

In an open project, the movie lands at the playhead on the front track if it fits, otherwise on a new track in front. The microphone lands on a new back track named **Microphone**.

As a new project, the canvas takes the movie's size and the format's frame rate, rounded to a whole number.

See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) for the full rules, and [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/) for a camera that's unplugged mid-take.

## With an agent

An agent names the camera and its format in words, and one that isn't there is refused with a list of what is. Its recording starts once the camera has settled, and its time counts from the camera's first frame. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/)
- [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)

---
title: The recorder panel
description: Set up a recording in the New Recording panel, from what to record and where it lands to what each control does and what the panel remembers.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

The New Recording panel holds every recording choice in one place: record a display, a window, a camera or the microphone, straight into a project.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording… on the Welcome window"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The macOS permission for what you record, asked for when you press Record."
/>

## Open the panel

Choose **File ▸ New Recording…** or press <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>, or click **New Recording…** on the [Welcome window](/projects/welcome-window/). You don't need a project open, and the menu item is always available.

There's one panel for the whole app. A recording doesn't belong to a project window, so it carries on if you close one.

While a recording runs, paused included, the same menu item reads **File ▸ Stop Recording** and <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> stops the recording. The Welcome window's button never stops one: during a screen recording it beeps, and during a camera recording or a voice-over it shows the panel again.

<Shot
  name="16-recorder-panel.panel"
  alt="The New Recording panel. From the top: Source set to Built-in Retina Display, the Include Frame Job windows and Record the camera too boxes, greyed Camera, Format and Layout rows, Microphone set to Off with a level meter, System Audio on, Cursor set to Separate, Show Clicks off, the Record shortcuts box, the When it lands boxes with Zoom in on clicks ticked, Rate at 60 fps, Size at Nominal (points) with a note reading 2056×1329 points, 4112×2658 pixels, and Record Into set to a project. Saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings sits at the bottom left, beside Close and Record."
/>

## Make a recording

<Steps>

1. Choose what to record in [**Source**](#choose-a-source).

2. Choose where it goes in [**Record Into**](#choose-where-it-lands).

3. Set any other [controls](#the-controls). Rows that don't apply to your source are greyed out.

4. Press **Record**. Frame Job checks the [permissions](/recording/permissions/) that source needs, then counts down from 3.

5. Stop when you're done. See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/).

</Steps>

**Close** closes the panel without recording.

A recording is saved as an ordinary movie or audio file in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, then imported like any other media, so every edit, effect and export works on it. It [lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) at the playhead of the project you chose, or opens as a new project.

## Choose a source

**Source** lists one row for each connected display, by name, and then three more.

| Row | What it records |
| --- | --- |
| A display's name | [The whole display](/recording/record-a-display/). |
| **Window…** | [One window](/recording/record-a-window/), which you pick with macOS's window picker. |
| **Camera** | [A camera on its own](/recording/record-a-camera/), with no screen. |
| **Microphone Only** | [A voice-over](/recording/voice-overs/): the microphone with no picture. |

It starts on the display you used last, or the main display if there isn't one. Every display is listed even before Frame Job has the Screen Recording permission, so the panel can open and tell you what's missing.

To record a camera as well as the screen, keep a display or **Window…** as the source and tick **Record the camera too**. See [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).

## Choose where it lands

**Record Into** lists **New Project** first, then every open project by name. It starts on the project in front, or **New Project** when none is open.

The row follows whichever project is in front until you choose a row yourself. After that it keeps your choice for as long as that project stays open, and if you close the project it goes back to following the one in front. If you choose **New Project**, it stays there.

The list updates every second while the panel is idle. From the press of **Record** to the landing it's frozen, so clicking into another project during a recording doesn't change where the recording goes.

**Record Into** is never remembered between launches.

## The controls

These are the panel's rows in order, with what each starts on before you've changed anything.

| Control | What it does | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Source** | [What to record](#choose-a-source). | The main display |
| **Include Frame Job windows** | [Puts Frame Job's own windows](/recording/record-a-display/#include-frame-job-windows) into a display recording and into the window picker's list. | Off |
| **Record the camera too** | [Records a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/). | Off |
| **Camera** | [Which camera to record](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-camera). | The Mac's preferred camera |
| **Format** | [The camera's size and frame rate](/recording/record-a-camera/#choose-a-format). | Best |
| **Preview** | [A live picture of the camera](/recording/record-a-camera/#check-the-picture). This row appears only when a camera is wanted. | |
| **Layout** | [Where the camera lands](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) beside the screen. | Corner |
| **Remove the camera's background when it lands** | [Cuts the person out](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/) of the camera's clips. | Off |
| **Microphone** | [**Off**, or a connected microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/), with a level meter beside it. | Off |
| **Enhance the microphone when it lands** | [Runs Enhance Voice](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the microphone's clips. | Off |
| **System Audio** | [Records what the Mac plays](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/). | On |
| **Cursor** | [Whether the pointer is drawn into the movie](/recording/cursor/): **Separate** or **In the picture**. | Separate |
| **Show Clicks** | [Marks each mouse click](/recording/cursor/). | Off |
| **Record shortcuts** | [Records the shortcuts you press](/recording/record-shortcuts/), and when you type, but never what you type. | Off |
| **When it lands:** **Zoom in on clicks** | [Runs Auto Zoom](/recording/when-it-lands/) on the screen clips. | On |
| **Show shortcuts** | [Adds shortcut overlays](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | On |
| **Speed up typing** | [Runs Speed Up Typing](/recording/when-it-lands/). Needs **Record shortcuts**. | Off |
| **Rate** | [The most frames per second](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) the file may hold, and a new project's frame rate. | 60 fps |
| **Size** | [Records at points or pixels](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size). | Nominal (points) |
| **Record Into** | [Where the recording lands](#choose-where-it-lands). | The project in front, else New Project |

## What greys out

Rows that don't apply to the chosen source grey out and keep their values, so nothing jumps and your settings are still there when you switch back.

| When | Greyed out |
| --- | --- |
| **Source** is **Microphone Only** | **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout**, the background box, **System Audio**, **Cursor**, **Show Clicks**, **Record shortcuts**, the three **When it lands:** boxes and **Size**. **Rate** stays live, because it sets a new project's frame rate. |
| **Source** is **Camera** | The same rows, except **Camera** and **Format**, which go live. **Rate** greys out as well, because a camera records at its format's rate. |
| **Record the camera too** is off, with a display or window | **Camera**, **Format**, **Layout** and the background box. |
| **Microphone** is **Off** | **Enhance the microphone when it lands**. |
| **Record shortcuts** is off | **Show shortcuts** and **Speed up typing**. |

**Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live for every source.

Every control locks from the press of **Record** until the recording has landed.

## The note under Size

A line under **Size** tells you what you'll get from the chosen source.

| Source | The note reads |
| --- | --- |
| A display | Both its sizes, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels` |
| A picked window | "the picked window's own size" |
| **Microphone Only** | "no picture — the microphone alone" |
| **Camera**, with **Format** on Best | For example `1760×1328 at 30 fps — the camera's best format` |
| **Camera**, with a format chosen | For example `1920×1080 at 30 fps — the chosen format` |
| **Camera**, with none connected | "no camera connected" |

## The footnote

The text at the bottom left of the panel shows where recordings are saved, for example `saved in ~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`.

When the panel stays up during a recording, as it does for a camera or a voice-over, the footnote shows the time instead: the coral **●** and the elapsed time while recording, or **❚❚** and the time held still while paused.

## What the panel remembers

The panel reopens as you left it, between launches. It keeps:

- the display, the microphone, the camera and the camera format
- **System Audio**, **Show Clicks** and **Cursor**
- **Rate** and **Size**
- every box: **Include Frame Job windows**, **Record the camera too**, **Remove the camera's background when it lands**, **Enhance the microphone when it lands**, **Record shortcuts** and the three **When it lands:** boxes
- **Layout**

A few things work differently:

- **Cursor** is remembered only once you choose it. Until then it shows Separate, and a choice you make holds for every source.
- The camera format is one choice for every camera. A camera that doesn't have it shows Best.
- A picked window, and **Camera** or **Microphone Only** as the **Source** row, last until you quit. The camera itself is remembered.
- **Record Into** isn't remembered.

A display that's no longer connected falls back to the main display, a microphone to **Off**, and a camera to the default camera.

## Keys in the panel

<kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Record** and <kbd>Esc</kbd> presses **Close**.

Those two buttons change as a recording goes on, and the keys go with them. During the countdown <kbd>Return</kbd> presses **Cancel**, and while a camera or a voice-over records it presses **Stop**. <kbd>Esc</kbd> always closes the panel, which ends a countdown but leaves a running recording going.

The panel takes the keyboard only when you open it with Frame Job active. Opened while another app is in front, it leaves the keyboard with that app, so <kbd>Return</kbd> goes there.

## How the panel floats

The panel is built to sit beside whatever you're about to record.

- It stays above other windows, and it doesn't hide when you switch to another app.
- Clicking it doesn't make Frame Job the active app, so your project windows don't jump over the app you're recording.
- Opened while Frame Job is in the background, it comes to the front without taking the keyboard, so your typing stays where it was.
- It opens in the centre of the screen. Drag it anywhere, and it stays there until you quit.
- It pushes itself back onto its display when the countdown or a note makes it taller, so **Cancel** never ends up under the Dock. Its top-left corner stays put unless the screen edge forces a move.

For a display or a window, the panel [leaves the screen](/recording/record-a-display/#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record) once the recording starts.

## With an agent

An agent doesn't use the panel. `record_screen` records for a set time, from 1 to 600 seconds, with no panel and no countdown, and answers once the recording has landed.

- The recording lands at the playhead on the front track of whatever is open, nest included, or on a new track in front when that one has no room. With no project open, it opens as a new untitled project.
- The tool never asks for a permission and never opens the window picker. A missing permission is refused by name, with the System Settings pane to go to, so grant it once from the panel. A Frame Job launched from a terminal runs under the terminal's permissions.
- The [assistant](/assistant/overview/) can't call it.

[Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/) has every argument, and the order its refusals come in.

## Related

- [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)

title: Record a display
description: Record everything on one display, choose its size and frame rate, and decide whether Frame Job's own windows appear in the picture.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a display when you want everything on one screen in the movie: a demo that moves between apps, or a tutorial with menus and dialogs.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording permission."
/>

## Record a display

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

2. Choose the display by name in **Source**. There's one row for each connected display, and the panel starts on the display you used last, or the main display.

3. Set [**Size**](#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](#choose-a-frame-rate), and anything else you want, such as the [microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/).

4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown the panel [leaves the screen](#where-the-panel-goes-while-you-record) and recording starts.

5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

</Steps>

The recording lands in the project you chose in **Record Into**. See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/).

## Choose a size

**Size** sets how many pixels the movie holds.

| Size | What you get |
| --- | --- |
| **Nominal (points)** | The display's point size. This is the default. |
| **Best (pixels)** | Every pixel: the point size times the display's scale, which is twice the points on a Retina display. |

The note under the row shows both for the chosen display, for example `1728×1117 points · 3456×2234 pixels`.

Choose **Best (pixels)** when small text has to stay sharp, and **Nominal (points)** for smaller files. An odd width or height is rounded up to an even number when the movie is encoded.

## Choose a frame rate

**Rate** is **30 fps** or **60 fps**, and starts on 60 fps. It does two things:

- It's the most frames per second the file may hold.
- It's the frame rate of a new project made from the recording.

It's a ceiling, not a promise. macOS delivers a new frame only when something on screen changes, so a mostly still screen gives a file with a low, uneven frame rate. That's the file doing its job and not a fault.

**Rate** greys out for **Camera**, which records at its format's rate. It stays live for **Microphone Only**, where it sets a new project's frame rate.

## Include Frame Job windows

Frame Job's own windows, such as the editor and the preview, are left out of a display recording. Tick **Include Frame Job windows** to put them in the picture, for example when you're recording a Frame Job tutorial. It's off by default.

- The recorder panel is never in the picture, even with the box ticked.
- Frame Job's own sound stays out either way, so you can play the timeline during a recording and it won't end up in the file.
- The box also decides whether Frame Job's windows appear in the [window picker](/recording/record-a-window/#which-windows-the-picker-lists).

## Where the panel goes while you record

The panel leaves the screen once a display or window recording starts, and the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) becomes your controls.

While the panel is away, <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> stops the recording rather than showing the panel, and the Welcome window's **New Recording…** button beeps.

After the recording lands, the panel comes back only if there's a note to show you, such as a problem with the microphone. Otherwise it stays away until you open it again.

The panel stays up for **Camera** and **Microphone Only**, which film nothing on screen.

## With an agent

An agent picks a display by number, with the main display as the default, and it can't name a display and a window at once. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record a window](/recording/record-a-window/)
- [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/)
- [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/)

title: Record a window
description: Pick one window with macOS's picker and record it alone, at its own size.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a window when only one app matters. The movie is that window alone, at its own size, with nothing else on your screen in it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Window…"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Screen Recording permission."
/>

## Record a window

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

2. Choose **Window…** in **Source**. macOS's window picker opens.

3. Click the window you want. **Source** now reads **Window (picked)**, and the note under **Size** reads "the picked window's own size".

4. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown the panel leaves the screen and recording starts.

5. Stop with the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/) or <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd>.

</Steps>

[**Size**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-size) and [**Rate**](/recording/record-a-display/#choose-a-frame-rate) work as they do for a display: **Nominal (points)** records the window at its point size, and **Best (pixels)** at every pixel.

If the window closes while you're recording, see [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/).

## Pick a different window

Choose **Window (picked)** again to open the picker and pick another window.

Choosing any other row in **Source** drops the pick. A pick lasts until you quit: close and reopen the panel and it's still there, but it's never remembered between launches.

## If you cancel the picker

Cancel the picker and **Source** goes back to the display you used last, or the main display. That's also true when you've already picked a window and choose the row again, so the earlier pick is gone.

If the picker can't open at all, **Source** goes back the same way and the panel reads "The window picker could not open: …" with the reason.

## Which windows the picker lists

The picker lists other apps' windows. Frame Job's own windows depend on **Include Frame Job windows**:

| Box | The picker lists |
| --- | --- |
| Off | None of Frame Job's windows |
| On | Frame Job's windows, but never the recorder panel |

The box only changes the next time the picker opens. A window you've already picked stays picked.

## Record needs a picked window

If you press **Record** while the row still reads **Window…**, with nothing picked, the panel says "Choose a window with Window… first, or pick a display." No countdown starts, so nothing wrong gets recorded.

## With an agent

An agent doesn't use the picker. It names a window by its system window id, and an id that doesn't name a window Frame Job can record is refused. It can't name a window and a display at once. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [The recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/)
- [Record a display](/recording/record-a-display/)
- [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/)
- [The cursor in a recording](/recording/cursor/)

title: Record a camera
description: Record a connected camera on its own, with no screen, and choose its format, check its picture and see where the movie lands.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Record a camera on its own when you want a piece to camera with no screen in it. Frame Job records the chosen camera at the chosen format's highest frame rate.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ New Recording…"
  keys="⌥⌘N"
  where="New Recording panel ▸ Source ▸ Camera"
  tools="record_screen"
  needs="The Camera permission, and the Microphone permission when you choose a microphone. Screen Recording isn't needed."
/>

## Record a camera on its own

<Steps>

1. Open the [recorder panel](/recording/recorder-panel/) with <kbd>⌥⌘N</kbd> and choose **Camera** in **Source**.

2. Choose the camera in [**Camera**](#choose-a-camera) and its size and frame rate in [**Format**](#choose-a-format).

3. Check the live picture in the [**Preview**](#check-the-picture) under **Format**.

4. Choose a microphone in **Microphone**, or leave it **Off** to record the camera alone. The microphone can be the camera's own, if macOS lists it, and it's recorded to its own file beside the movie.

5. Choose where it goes in **Record Into**.

6. Press **Record**. After a 3, 2, 1 countdown recording starts, and the panel [stays up](#stop-and-pause-from-the-panel).

</Steps>

With no camera connected, pressing **Record** says "No camera is connected."

**System Audio**, **Show Clicks**, **Size**, **Include Frame Job windows**, **Rate** and the other rows for the screen grey out, and keep their values for next time. **Microphone** and **Record Into** stay live.

To record a camera and the screen at once, see [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/).

## Choose a camera

**Camera** lists each connected camera by name, or a single row, **None connected**, when there isn't one. An iPhone used as a Continuity Camera has "(Continuity Camera)" after its name.

It starts on the camera you used last, then the Mac's preferred camera, then the first built-in camera, then the first one connected.

The row is live when **Source** is **Camera** or **Record the camera too** is ticked, and greyed out otherwise.

## Choose a format

**Format** sets the size and frame rate the camera records at.

**Best** comes first and names what it will pick, for example **Best (1760×1328 at 30 fps)**. The camera's other formats follow, written like **1920×1080 at 30 fps**. Sizes wider than tall come first, then square, then taller than wide, each largest first.

Each format records at its highest frame rate, so you can't choose a lower rate within a format's range.

It starts on the format you used last when the chosen camera has it, otherwise **Best**. The row is live and greyed out at the same times as **Camera**.

## What Best picks

**Best** is the largest format wider than tall that reaches 30 fps or more, at that format's highest rate. If two formats are the same size, the higher rate wins, and then the one the camera lists first.

If no format wider than tall reaches 30 fps, Frame Job looks at every shape the same way. If none of those does either, it uses the format the camera is already set to.

## Check the picture

The **Preview** under **Format** shows the chosen camera live at the chosen format, as the movie will record it. It isn't mirrored, so you see what's being filmed, and the whole picture is fitted inside the well.

The row appears only when **Source** is **Camera** or **Record the camera too** is ticked, and it stays live through the countdown and the recording.

Sometimes it shows words instead of a picture.

| The preview reads | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "No camera is connected." | There's no camera to show. |
| "The preview shows once Frame Job may use the camera." | Frame Job doesn't have the Camera permission yet. Showing the panel never asks for it. Pressing **Record** does. |
| "The camera is recording." | An agent is recording the camera. The picture comes back when it's done. |
| Another sentence | The reason the camera couldn't start. To try again, choose another source and then **Camera**, or close and reopen the panel. |

## How the camera warms up

The camera starts as soon as the panel shows it, so it's ready before you record, and its light stays on while the panel shows **Camera**. Choosing another source turns it off, unless **Record the camera too** is ticked there, and so does closing the panel.

A camera that's starting cold can take a moment to run at its full rate. Frame Job gives it up to a second, in the countdown, so the recording starts steady, and then holds the camera to the chosen format and rate for the whole recording.

If it never settles, the recording begins anyway, and the note when it lands names the rate it ran at, for example "The camera ran at 24.3 fps, not its 30, in the 1 s it was given to settle; the recording began anyway."

## Stop and pause from the panel

The panel stays on screen while a camera records, because nothing on screen is being filmed.

- The controls lock and the microphone's level meter stays live.
- The [footnote](/recording/recorder-panel/#the-footnote) shows **●** or **❚❚** with the time.
- **Record** reads **Stop**, with a **Pause** or **Resume** button beside it.

Choose **Close** and the panel goes away, but the recording carries on under the [menu-bar item](/recording/menu-bar-item/). See [Start, pause and stop](/recording/pause-and-stop/) for the other ways to stop.

## Where a camera recording lands

The movie is saved as `Camera Recording 2026-10-26 at 17.14.33.mov` in `~/Movies/Frame Job Recordings`, with any microphone in its own `.m4a` file beside it.

In an open project, the movie lands at the playhead on the front track if it fits, otherwise on a new track in front. The microphone lands on a new back track named **Microphone**.

As a new project, the canvas takes the movie's size and the format's frame rate, rounded to a whole number.

See [Where a recording lands](/recording/where-it-lands/) for the full rules, and [When a recording stops on its own](/recording/when-a-recording-stops/) for a camera that's unplugged mid-take.

## With an agent

An agent names the camera and its format in words, and one that isn't there is refused with a list of what is. Its recording starts once the camera has settled, and its time counts from the camera's first frame. See [Record with `record_screen`](/mcp/record-screen/).

## Related

- [Record a camera beside the screen](/recording/camera-beside-the-screen/)
- [System audio and the microphone](/recording/system-audio-and-microphone/)
- [Recording permissions](/recording/permissions/)
- [Recording files and formats](/recording/files-and-formats/)
